title: Render position uncertainty on the maze
description: You evaluate a Gaussian over maze cells and mark the true position.

steps.description: You accept scalar or size-one dimensions and convert them to Python integers. The Gaussian helper also reshapes its mean and covariance to position dimensions.
You symmetrize the covariance and floor its eigenvalues at eps. Scaled grid coordinates then enter the Gaussian density formula.

steps.question: Does visualization normalization make the cell values sum to one?
steps.answer: It divides by the largest finite positive value, so the peak becomes one. It also zeros wall cells before this normalization.

steps.description: You validate the wall mask and display the grid with a Relative Probability color bar. The true position becomes a red X after conversion from world units to cells.
You create one heatmap per estimate from xs and its position covariance in Ps. Each map is stored and displayed with the corresponding true position.
